themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints surged to 72 THIS WEEK vs. 19.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks—a 267% spike (z-score: 5.37)—suggesting a sudden deterioration in Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights road surfaces coinciding with winter weather transition.
evidence: 72 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 19.6 weekly baseline (8-week average)
267% spike from baseline with z-score of 5.37 (high statistical significance)
Coincides with seasonal transition and potential freeze-thaw damage patterns
Long-standing budget request for 'Other transportation infrastructure requests' suggests chronic underinvestment
reporting_angles: Inspect specific streets mentioned in complaints; photograph potholes and assess damage severity
Interview residents about commute disruption and safety risks (wheelchairs, bicycles, elderly pedestrians)
Cross-reference with DOT maintenance schedules and budget allocation to this district

themes_detail.label: Mysterious Damaged Tree Spike
themes_detail.summary: Damaged tree complaints exploded to 15 THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly average—a 700% spike (z-score: 8.54)—indicating either acute environmental event (ice storm, high winds) or coordinated reporting of pre-existing neglect in the district.
evidence: 15 damaged tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly baseline (8-week average)
700% increase with z-score of 8.54 (extremely statistically significant)
Parks budget request repeatedly filed for 'New equipment for maintenance' suggests chronic understaffing
Could indicate weather event or sudden visibility/tipping point on deferred maintenance
reporting_angles: Visit major parks (Fort Greene Park, Brooklyn Bridge Park vicinity) to visually verify tree damage extent
Interview Parks Department on whether weather event triggered complaints or if backlog is finally being reported
Assess whether tree maintenance funding and staffing levels match complaint volume

themes_detail.label: Sanitation System Distress
themes_detail.summary: Sewer complaints spiked to 20 LAST WEEK vs. 3.8 weekly average—a 433% increase (z-score: 8.46)—paired with street sweeping complaints up 643% to 13 THIS WEEK (vs. 1.8 avg), suggesting coordinated sanitation infrastructure failure or acute environmental event.
evidence: Sewer complaints: 20 last week vs. 3.8 weekly baseline (433% spike, z-score: 8.46)
Street sweeping complaints: 13 THIS WEEK vs. 1.8 weekly baseline (643% spike, z-score: 7.61)
Litter basket requests: 14 last week vs. 1.4 weekly baseline (918% spike, z-score: 7.31)
DEP budget request repeatedly filed for 'Other expense budget request' suggests chronic underfunding
reporting_angles: Interview DEP on whether sewer backups or flooding events occurred; obtain emergency response logs
Talk to residents and businesses in affected areas about odors, backup, or surface flooding
Investigate whether lack of street cleaning resources is allowing litter/debris to clog storm drains and sewers

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Outbreak
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints jumped to 4 TWO WEEKS AGO from 0.1 weekly average—a 3100% spike (z-score: 11.72)—potentially signaling organized poster campaigns, missing permit enforcement, or gang/political activity in the district.
evidence: Illegal posting complaints: 4 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (3100% spike, z-score: 11.72)
Asbestos complaints also spiked 967% TWO WEEKS AGO (4 vs. 0.4 avg, z-score: 7.49)—may be coincidental or indicate construction/demolition disruption
High z-score suggests statistically anomalous event rather than normal variation
reporting_angles: Canvass district for posted materials; photograph and catalog content (political, commercial, gang-related)
Interview Parks/Sanitation on enforcement patterns—are they responding to complaints or is posting outpacing removal?
Check if spike correlates with election season, construction projects, or other district events

themes_detail.label: Noise Surge on Streets
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped to 46 THIS WEEK vs. 14.4 weekly average—a 220% spike (z-score: 5.53)—on top of the already-high baseline of 1,814 residential noise complaints over 90 days, suggesting acute noise source or event in the district.
evidence: Street/sidewalk noise complaints: 46 THIS WEEK vs. 14.4 weekly baseline (220% spike, z-score: 5.53)
Residential noise complaints: 1,814 total over 90 days (second-highest complaint category after illegal parking)
Spike suggests new point-source noise (construction, event, transit disruption) rather than ambient increase
reporting_angles: Identify source: active construction sites, transit delays/congestion, outdoor events, or commercial venues operating longer hours
Interview residents in highest-complaint zones about noise type (jackhammering, traffic, music, etc.) and timing
Cross-reference with DOB permits (77 new buildings filed in last 90 days) to assess construction activity
